title: [Chapitre] I. Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques) : notes manuscrites (05/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a fresh start, numbered '2', of the axiomatic set-up drafted on the previous page. Grothendieck is trying to describe 1-dimensional topological 'forms' (graph-like spaces: arcs, circles, branched curves) purely combinatorially, without point-set topology. That fits the programme 'Vers une géométrie des formes (topologiques)', which is close in spirit to the tame-topology ideas of Esquisse d'un programme.

A 'model' consists of the following data.
(1) Two base sets: L, the set of 'lieux' (places), and S, the set of 'segments'.
(2) A map S → P(L), I ↦ Ĩ, giving the places lying on the segment I. Equivalently, an incidence relation between S and L.
(3) A map ∂ : S → P_2(L), the 2-element subsets of L, with ∂I ⊂ Ĩ. These are the two endpoints.
Axioms are still to come.

NB: he does not know whether a segment should be determined by (Ĩ, ∂I), i.e. whether S → P(L) × P_2(L) should be injective. This repeats NB 3 of the previous page. A dated marginal addition ('7.6.', presumably 7 June 1986, two days after the folder date 05/06/1986) seems to say there is no reason not to identify S with a subset of P(L) (or of P(L) × P_2(L)). In other words, segments could simply be certain subsets of places.

Terminology:
- The elements of ∂I are the endpoints of I.
- The elements of Ĩ∖∂I (written Ĩ° on the next page) are the interior places of I.
- A place is regular if it is interior to some segment, and singular (or critical, or a branching place) otherwise.
- L_r = ⋃_{I∈S} (Ĩ∖∂I) and L_s = L∖L_r.

Immediate consequence: Ĩ ∩ L_s ⊂ ∂I for every I. A segment meets the singular locus only at its endpoints. Hence segments are meant to be the 'edges' of a stratification. The singular places play the role of vertices; regular places form the 1-dimensional open stratum.

The next page builds on this:
- a 'specialization' relation from regular places x to singular endpoints y of a segment through x, borrowing the Zariski/stratification vocabulary;
- decomposition axioms: cutting a segment at an interior place;
- gluing axioms: joining two segments at a common regular endpoint;
- density/finiteness axioms: every finite subset of Ĩ° lies inside a subsegment contained in Ĩ°.
errors: There is a hidden assumption in the definition of 'singular'. If segments were arbitrary arcs, the centre of a tripod would be interior to the arc joining two legs, hence 'regular', contradicting its intended role as a branching place. The definition only works if segments are implicitly unbranched arcs, i.e. their interior places have no branching. Nothing on this page enforces this; it must come from axioms still to be written (the gluing axiom on the next page only glues at regular places, which is consistent with this intention).

The question of whether I is determined by (Ĩ, ∂I) is left open. For a circle with two marked places x, y, the two arcs have the same ∂ but different Ĩ, so Ĩ separates them. A genuine failure of injectivity would only arise for parallel edges if places are coarse. The margin note leans toward taking S ⊂ P(L), which is harmless here.
Minor: Ĩ ∩ L_s ⊂ ∂I is a tautology of the definitions, not a result.

ideas.what: Combinatorial/incidence description of 1-dimensional topological forms by a set of places and a set of segments with incidence and a 2-element boundary map
ideas.modern_name: Incidence structure / abstract 1-complex; arc-structure on a topological graph; close to betweenness/segment axiomatics (Hilbert's order axioms, median algebras, R-tree axioms)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Hilbert, Veblen for order axioms; graph-theory incidence formalisms; Morgan–Shalen/Chiswell for tree axiomatics)
ideas.where_published: Only the general aspiration toward a 'geometry of forms' and tame topology appears (Esquisse d'un programme, Récoltes et Semailles); this axiomatics is unpublished as far as I know

ideas.what: Regular vs singular (branching/critical) places, with segments meeting the singular locus only at endpoints
ideas.modern_name: Stratification of a topological graph into vertices (0-strata) and open edges (1-strata)

ideas.what: Option of identifying segments with subsets of places (S ⊂ P(L))

deep.surprise_reason: Foundational bookkeeping for an axiomatic theory of 1-dimensional forms: base sets, incidence map, boundary map and the regular/singular split. It is historically interesting as part of the little-known 1986 'géométrie des formes' project, which probably merits only a historical note. The content of this page is routine and close to standard incidence and stratification formalisms. The more substantive axioms (decomposition, gluing, specialization) are on the next page.
transcription_corrections: Margin note begins with '7.6.', most likely a date (7 June 1986), followed by roughly: 'On ne voit pas pourquoi (si I est connu quand on connaît Ĩ) on ne pourrait identifier S à une partie de P(L)'. The words 'non injectif' also seem to appear. The transcription's '{+7.6. On ne voit pas pourquoi ...+}' is fragmentary.
NB line reads approximately: 'J'ignore s'il faut supposer que I est connu quand on connaît Ĩ et ∂I, i.e. s'il faut supposer I ↦ (Ĩ, ∂I) : S → P(L) × P_2(L) injectif.'
Line 3 reads 'Une application ∂ : S → P_2(L), I ↦ ∂I, telle que ∂I ⊂ Ĩ'. The 'I ↦ ∂I' is written above the line.
In 'les éléments de Ĩ ∖ ∂I', there is an underlined/struck 'Ĩ' variant above; the meaning is 'les lieux intérieurs au segment'.
The singular definition reads 'singulier (ou critique, ou lieu de branchement) sinon'. A struck '(intérieur)' / '(ou intérieur)' variant sits under 'Un lieu', with 'à un segment' added below it.
